text: Meanwhile Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down there. Just then the redeemer he had spoken of came by, and Boaz said, "Come over here, friend, and sit down." So he turned aside and sat down.
Boaz then took ten of the elders of the town and said, "Sit down here," and they sat down.
He said to the redeemer, "Naomi, who has come back from the country of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

I thought I should bring the matter to your attention and say: Buy it in the presence of those sitting here and of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it. But if you will not, tell me, so that I may know—for there is no one to redeem it but you, and I come after you." And he said, "I will redeem it."

versions.text: I thought I should bring the matter to your attention and say: Buy it, here in the presence of those seated here and of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it. But if you will not, tell me, so I know—for there is no one to redeem it but you, and I come after you." And he said, "I will redeem it."
versions.explanation: "here ... here" is redundant and stumbles when read aloud; also "so that I may know" better renders the cohortative וְאֵדְעָה and flows more smoothly than the clipped "so I know."

text: Then Boaz said, "On the day you buy the field from Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the widow of the dead man, in order to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance."
At that the redeemer said, "Then I cannot redeem it for myself, or I would ruin my own inheritance. Take over my right of redemption yourself, for I cannot redeem it."

versions.text: At that the redeemer said, "Then I cannot redeem it for myself; I would ruin my own inheritance. Take over my right of redemption yourself, for I cannot redeem it."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew פֶּן ("lest") expresses purpose/consequence; the semicolon leaves the two clauses logically disconnected, and "or I would" restores the causal link without adding words.

text: Now in earlier times in Israel, this was the custom concerning redemption and exchange, to confirm any transaction: a man would take off his sandal and hand it to the other party. This was the way of attesting a matter in Israel.
So the redeemer said to Boaz, "Buy it yourself," and he took off his sandal.
Then Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have bought from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech and everything that belonged to Kilion and Mahlon.

And I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon's widow, as my wife, in order to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance, so that his name will not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his town. You are witnesses today."

All the people at the gate and the elders said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is entering your house like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and be renowned in Bethlehem.
And through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman, may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah."
So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went to her, and the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.
Then the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without a redeemer! May his name be renowned in Israel.
He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and who is worth more to you than seven sons, has given him birth."
Naomi took the child, laid him on her lap, and became his nurse.
The women of the neighborhood gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
This is the line of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron,
Hezron the father of Ram, Ram the father of Amminadab,
Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmon,

versions.text: Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmah,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew alternates between Salmah (v. 20) and Salmon (v. 21) for the same man. In a genealogy meant to be read aloud, two different names in consecutive lines will sound like two different people. Using "Salmon" consistently, with a footnote noting that the Hebrew of this verse reads "Salmah," preserves accuracy and aids the listener.

text: Salmon the father of Boaz, Boaz the father of Obed,
Obed the father of Jesse, and Jesse the father of David.
